Queue::kind, Queue::Kind, Queue::kind_name, is_series, is_note, is_timeline, is_duration¶

Back to Queue API Reference

Signature¶

enum class Queue::Kind : std::uint8_t { Series, Note, Timeline, Duration };

Kind kind() const noexcept;
std::string_view kind_name() const noexcept;
static constexpr std::string_view kind_name(Kind k) noexcept;

bool is_series() const noexcept;
bool is_note() const noexcept;
bool is_timeline() const noexcept;
bool is_duration() const noexcept;

What It Does¶

kind() reports which of the four payload types a Queue is actually holding, as a Queue::Kind enum value. kind_name() gives the same answer as a human-readable string – "Series", "Note", "Timeline", or "Duration" – and the static overload converts an arbitrary Kind value to its name without needing a Queue instance at all. is_series(), is_note(), is_timeline(), and is_duration() are convenience shorthands for kind() == Queue::Kind::X, one per kind, none of them mutually exclusive with the others being false – exactly one is ever true for a given Queue.

None of these methods can throw, and none of them require knowing the payload type in advance – they are the methods you call first, before deciding how to handle a Queue you were just handed.

Parameters¶

k (Kind, static overload only)

The kind value to name.

Returns¶

kind() returns a Queue::Kind. kind_name() (both overloads) returns a std::string_view into a function-local string literal, valid for the program’s lifetime. The four is_* methods return bool.

Examples¶

Example 1. kind(), kind_name(), and the static kind_name(Kind) overload, read directly off a Series-holding Queue.

pluss::Queue q(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}));
std::cout << "kind() == Queue::Kind::Series: " << (q.kind() == pluss::Queue::Kind::Series) << '\n';
std::cout << "kind_name(): " << q.kind_name() << '\n';
std::cout << "static kind_name(Kind::Note): " << pluss::Queue::kind_name(pluss::Queue::Kind::Note) << '\n';
std::cout << "static kind_name(Kind::Timeline): " << pluss::Queue::kind_name(pluss::Queue::Kind::Timeline) << '\n';
std::cout << "static kind_name(Kind::Duration): " << pluss::Queue::kind_name(pluss::Queue::Kind::Duration) << '\n';

Output¶

kind() == Queue::Kind::Series: true
kind_name(): Series
static kind_name(Kind::Note): Note
static kind_name(Kind::Timeline): Timeline
static kind_name(Kind::Duration): Duration

The static overload names any Kind value directly – useful for printing a kind you got from somewhere other than a live Queue, such as a stored enum value.

Example 2. is_series()/is_note()/is_timeline()/is_duration() on a Series-holding and a Note-holding Queue. Exactly one is true in each case.

pluss::Queue q(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}));
pluss::Queue note_q(pluss::make_note({"x"}));
std::cout << "series.is_series(): " << q.is_series() << '\n';
std::cout << "series.is_note(): " << q.is_note() << '\n';
std::cout << "note.is_note(): " << note_q.is_note() << '\n';
std::cout << "note.is_series(): " << note_q.is_series() << '\n';
std::cout << "note.is_timeline(): " << note_q.is_timeline() << '\n';
std::cout << "note.is_duration(): " << note_q.is_duration() << '\n';

Output¶

series.is_series(): true
series.is_note(): false
note.is_note(): true
note.is_series(): false
note.is_timeline(): false
note.is_duration(): false
